about: signals-v3 M2 (T2.3): the golden triage cases of PLAN.md success criterion 2, cut from PUBLIC rows of live build 20261013.1. Each golden member's full history is included (point in time), plus every row of the S-3 windows the golden cases read. Signals are the live artifact's active records, verbatim: every per-row signal of a golden member whose triggering row is in the slice, and the golden S-3 clusters (SPCX purchases from 2026-06-12 and the ten clusters Tuberville's 2026-08-05 filings completed). Other S-3 clusters are left out because their other members' filings are not in the slice.

rows.source: live build 20261013.1 public congress feed parts (/congress/data/feed/*.v1.json)
rows.note: rows verbatim, columns in txn_cols order

signals.note: active records verbatim; identities maps each per-row signal id to its triggering txnId, verified by the test against kind:fnv1a64(txnId)

committees.note: memberships of the slice's members only; the snapshot window is the table's own

issuers.note: every in-window ticker of the slice that the ticker map resolves to one CIK with an issuer_sic row

taxonomy.taxonomy_source: SIC division structure, Standard Industrial Classification Manual (1987), OMB / U.S. DOL; as used by SEC EDGAR
taxonomy.license_note: U.S. federal government work — public domain (17 U.S.C. §105)

artifact.lifecycleNote: this build continues the previous one: a signal keeps the same id and the date it was first seen for as long as it stays in the window. A signal that is no longer in the window — amended away, or no longer matching — is kept in the file rather than deleted, marked as no longer current and labelled with the build it left in.
artifact.compaction: signals whose filed date predates the 90-day window are compacted out of the artifact entirely; a device cursor older than coverage_from is a coverage gap the UI must state
artifact.lagCaveat: PTRs are filed up to 45 days after the trade (later when late) — at read time the position may have changed or closed; a signal describes a disclosure, never a current holding.
